hypotheses.name: Basement-interface gravity mass-balance residual
hypotheses.physical_signature: Fit a simple basement-interface forward gravity response from Band 15 to Band 13 using training spatial blocks only, then test whether a localized, persistent cross-strike gravity residual remains after broad basement relief is accounted for. Freeze density contrast, filtering, and edge treatment before holdout evaluation; compare the residual against raw gravity and basement-gradient controls.
hypotheses.catalogue_missing_rationale: A buried basement displacement could leave a density step beneath basin fill without a mapped surface scarp, while a broad basin response is absorbed by the forward component. This remains a hypothesis, not direct evidence of fault displacement.
hypotheses.novelty: A prior review proposed this exact forward-residual family, but no executable forward-gravity mass-balance residual or run card was found in this checkout. Existing H86E-SPBT pairs Band 13 and Band 15 steps; H86H-PSTD uses gravity-tensor features; the now-executed H86K-PSC uses a Hessian saddle/ridge score. None is this frozen physical forward-model residual test. Band 15 is gravity-derived, so it is not independent corroboration and circularity must be tested.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Lateral sediment-density changes, errors or smoothing in the gravity-derived basement-depth surface, and model-edge ringing.
hypotheses.expected_holdout_potential: Highest qualitative priority, but only moderate confidence: removing a broad basin component might expose a narrower residual, while dependence of Band 15 on gravity can make the residual circular or unstable.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: High; requires verified units and sign conventions, a fold-safe forward model, stability analysis, and matched raw-gravity/basement controls.
hypotheses.falsifier: The residual does not improve paired spatial-block HOLDOUT-DTI over both raw-gravity and basement-gradient controls, or its apparent signal disappears under plausible density contrasts and boundary conditions.

hypotheses.name: Gravity step-versus-compact-source shape test
hypotheses.physical_signature: At several frozen scales, compare normalized horizontal derivative width and signed east/south gradient patterns with simple extended-step and compact-source responses. Band 11 is a verified signed southward directional derivative and Band 18 a signed eastward derivative; neither should be treated as a conventional vertical-gravity derivative. Band 5 is the horizontal gradient magnitude.
hypotheses.catalogue_missing_rationale: An extended buried basement step could generate a coherent cross-strike response that is not captured by a single gradient maximum; rejecting compact-source-like anomalies may favor long, concealed discontinuities without using catalogue distance.
hypotheses.novelty: A 2026-10-23 review proposed the source-shape comparison, but no explicit step-versus-compact likelihood or response-ratio model was found in scripts/ or src/. H86F-GZZD and H86H-PSTD use gravity derivatives/tensors, and H86K-PSC now uses Hessian saddle/ridge topology, but none implements this explicit competing-source model comparison.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: An elongated intrusive contact, basin-margin facies change, or overlapping compact sources that happen to form a linear gradient corridor.
hypotheses.expected_holdout_potential: Low-to-medium qualitative potential; shape consistency may reject some isolated bodies, but a long lithologic contact can mimic a fault step.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium; requires scale-matched forward templates, verified coordinate/sign conventions, and sensitivity analysis to source depth and bandwidth.
hypotheses.falsifier: Step-source likelihood fails to outperform compact/contact controls on paired spatial-block HOLDOUT-DTI or changes rank materially across reasonable filter scales.

hypotheses.name: Conductivity-neck topology conditioned on dilatation
hypotheses.physical_signature: Track narrow conductive connections across a frozen threshold-persistence range, then test whether the necks co-locate with positive dilatation and coherent shear compared with conductivity-only, strain-only, and spatially randomized controls. This single surface-conductance band is not depth-resolved magnetotellurics.
hypotheses.catalogue_missing_rationale: A concealed fluid-permeability pathway could connect broader conductive zones without a surface scarp; using neck persistence rather than a conductivity maximum is intended to emphasize narrow pathways that raw-halo methods may suppress.
hypotheses.novelty: This conductivity-neck idea also appears as an H86K-CNT reserve in the merged H86K-PSC preregistration, but that entry is RESERVE and has no execution/run card. No threshold-persistent conductive-component neck extraction conditioned on dilatation was found in scripts/ or src/. Existing CTHB/FVMB/MCSP-style features use conductivity gradients, margins, or halos; they do not construct this exact topology test.
hypotheses.non_fault_mimic: Saline playa sediments, clay-rich paleochannels, or gridding/interpolation bottlenecks that connect conductive patches.
hypotheses.expected_holdout_potential: Lowest qualitative priority because surface conductivity is nonspecific; any benefit is conditional on stable topology and independent strain corroboration.
hypotheses.implementation_cost: Medium; multi-threshold connectivity, width controls, and randomized-neck nulls are needed.
hypotheses.falsifier: Neck features fail to beat both conductivity-only and strain-only controls, or their topology is unstable across the preregistered threshold range.

required_before_any_experiment: An explicit single assigned method paragraph; the current request has none.
The actual shared cached feature stack with preprocessing and visible-mask identity; native-band rebuilding is not an acceptable substitute.
The repository's fail-closed protocol disposition; do not bypass the literal witness stop or modify uniqueness thresholds.
A complete current same-grid registry and explicit treatment of incompatible registry entries.
Frozen buffered whole-segment hide-and-recover folds; derive catalogue features from visible faults only and mask visible pixels exactly.
Run isolated-feature leakage canaries before trust; discriminative AUC above 0.90 is a stop pending proof.
Use the shared evaluate_holdout.py, pooled DTI with alpha 0.2, beta 0.8, and a 300 m triangular kernel; report evaluator, withheld-positive count, and 95% CI.
Measure rank correlation before placement and 3-pixel dot overlap on the final dots against the complete registry; stop at rho > 0.90 or overlap > 0.70.
Stop after at most three experiments or two hours, and do not select a weekly submission slot here.
